swaps.plainSentence: The line graph shows the value of online and in-store retail sales in one country between 2014 and 2024.
swaps.formalSentence: The line graph illustrates the value of online and in-store retail sales in one country between 2014 and 2024.

formal: over the ten-year period from 2014 to 2024

swaps.formalSentence: The line graph illustrates the value of online and in-store retail sales in one country over the period 2014–2024.
swaps.note: Paraphrase the time frame: over the period X–Y.

swaps.plainSentence: The line graph illustrates how much money people spent on online and in-store shopping in one country over the period 2014–2024.
swaps.formalSentence: The line graph illustrates consumer spending on online and in-store shopping in one country over the period 2014–2024.
swaps.note: Turn 'how much money' into a noun phrase.

swaps.plainSentence: The line graph compares sales made online with sales made in shops in one country over the period 2014–2024.
swaps.formalSentence: The line graph compares sales made online with sales made in physical stores in one country over the period 2014–2024.
swaps.note: Paraphrase the topic nouns, not just the verb.

swaps.plainSentence: The numbers are in billions of pounds.
swaps.formalSentence: All figures are given in billions of pounds.
swaps.note: Optional second intro sentence that states the unit.

swaps.plainSentence: Overall, we can see that both channels changed dramatically in 2020, moving in opposite directions.
swaps.formalSentence: Overall, it is evident that both channels changed dramatically in 2020, moving in opposite directions.

traps.text: In conclusion, we can see that

swaps.note: Overview opener. No figures in the overview.

swaps.plainSentence: Online sales went up across the period as a whole, despite a sharp fall after their peak.
swaps.formalSentence: Online sales followed an upward trend across the period as a whole, despite a sharp fall after their peak.
swaps.note: Describe the whole-period trend; details go in the body.

swaps.plainSentence: In-store sales were bigger than online sales in every year except one.
swaps.formalSentence: In-store sales exceeded online sales in every year except one.
swaps.note: No preposition after exceed / outstrip / surpass.

swaps.plainSentence: In-store sales went up and down in the first half of the period before falling sharply in 2020.
swaps.formalSentence: In-store sales fluctuated in the first half of the period before falling sharply in 2020.
swaps.note: Small ups and downs = fluctuated.

swaps.plainSentence: The most important thing is that online sales briefly overtook in-store sales in 2020.
swaps.formalSentence: The most striking feature is that online sales briefly overtook in-store sales in 2020.
swaps.note: Second overview sentence: one standout feature, no figures.

swaps.plainSentence: By contrast, in-store sales went down overall, despite a partial recovery after 2020.
swaps.formalSentence: By contrast, in-store sales saw an overall decline, despite a partial recovery after 2020.

traps.why: too strong for the whole period

swaps.note: Contrast the second line in the overview, still without numbers.

formal: At the beginning of the period
swaps.plainSentence: At the start, online sales climbed gradually, rising by just £9 billion in three years.
swaps.formalSentence: At the beginning of the period, online sales climbed gradually, rising by just £9 billion in three years.
swaps.note: Body 1 opener: anchor the reader in time.

swaps.plainSentence: In 2014, online sales were £20 billion.
swaps.formalSentence: In 2014, online sales stood at £20 billion.
swaps.note: Use 'stood at' for the first figure of a line.

swaps.plainSentence: Online sales went up slowly from £20 billion in 2014 to £29 billion in 2017.
swaps.formalSentence: Online sales climbed steadily from £20 billion in 2014 to £29 billion in 2017.

traps.why: too strong for a slow rise

swaps.note: Slow, even rise = climbed steadily / rose gradually.

swaps.plainSentence: Between 2017 and 2020, online sales went up a lot, reaching £80 billion.
swaps.formalSentence: Between 2017 and 2020, online sales surged, reaching £80 billion.
swaps.note: Steep, fast rise = surged / rose sharply.

swaps.plainSentence: This was a big increase of £51 billion in just three years.
swaps.formalSentence: This was a dramatic increase of £51 billion in just three years.
swaps.note: Noun form: a dramatic increase = rose dramatically.

swaps.plainSentence: Online sales reached their highest point of £80 billion in 2020.
swaps.formalSentence: Online sales peaked at £80 billion in 2020.
swaps.note: The top of a line: peaked at / reached a peak of.

swaps.plainSentence: In the following year, however, online sales went down a lot to £50 billion.
swaps.formalSentence: In the following year, however, online sales plummeted to £50 billion.

traps.why: too weak for such a big fall

swaps.note: Steep fall = plummeted / plunged; small fall = dipped.

swaps.plainSentence: Thereafter, they stayed the same at just under £50 billion for the rest of the period.
swaps.formalSentence: Thereafter, they levelled off at just under £50 billion for the rest of the period.
swaps.note: British spelling: levelled, stabilised.

swaps.plainSentence: About in-store sales, the figure fluctuated between £100 billion and £105 billion from 2014 to 2018.
swaps.formalSentence: Turning to in-store sales, the figure fluctuated between £100 billion and £105 billion from 2014 to 2018.
swaps.note: Body 2 opener: signal the switch to the second line.

swaps.plainSentence: Between 2014 and 2018, in-store sales stayed at about £103 billion.
swaps.formalSentence: Between 2014 and 2018, in-store sales hovered around £103 billion.
swaps.note: Small moves around one level = hovered around.

swaps.plainSentence: In 2019, in-store sales went down a bit to £99 billion.
swaps.formalSentence: In 2019, in-store sales dipped to £99 billion.

traps.why: too strong for a small fall

swaps.note: Small fall = dipped / declined slightly.

swaps.plain: went to its lowest point of
swaps.plainSentence: In 2020, the figure went to its lowest point of £62 billion.
swaps.formalSentence: In 2020, the figure hit a low of £62 billion.
swaps.note: The bottom of a line: hit a low of / bottomed out at.

swaps.plainSentence: This was the only year in which online sales went higher than in-store sales.
swaps.formalSentence: This was the only year in which online sales overtook in-store sales.
swaps.note: Where two lines cross: overtook / surpassed.

swaps.plainSentence: However, in-store sales quickly got back to £85 billion in 2021.
swaps.formalSentence: However, in-store sales quickly recovered to £85 billion in 2021.
swaps.note: A rise after a low = recovered to / rebounded to.

swaps.plainSentence: After that, in-store sales rose gradually to reach £92 billion in 2024.
swaps.formalSentence: Subsequently, in-store sales rose gradually to reach £92 billion in 2024.
swaps.note: Move the story forward in time.

swaps.plainSentence: By 2024, there was a big difference between the two channels, with in-store sales almost double online sales.
swaps.formalSentence: By 2024, there was a considerable gap between the two channels, with in-store sales almost double online sales.

traps.why: wrong meaning: the gap was large

swaps.note: Closing comparison of the two lines at the end.

steps.best: The line graph illustrates how much electricity one country produced from coal, gas, nuclear power and wind over the period 1995–2020, measured in terawatt hours (TWh).

others.why: copies the question word for word

others.text: The line graph is illustrating about how much electricity was made by coal, gas, nuclear and wind since 1995 to 2020.

steps.best: Overall, it is evident that the country shifted away from coal towards gas and wind, while nuclear output remained broadly stable.

others.text: Overall, coal fell from 120 TWh to 20 TWh, while wind rose to 80 TWh.
others.why: figures belong in the body, not the overview

others.text: In conclusion, coal went down and gas and wind went up.
others.why: no 'In conclusion' in Task 1; plain verbs

steps.best: The most striking feature is the dramatic rise of wind power, which went from virtually nothing to become the second-largest source by the end of the period.

others.text: In 1995, coal was the most, with 120 TWh, four times more than gas.

others.text: In 1995, coal was by far the dominant source, generating 120 TWh, twice as much as gas (30 TWh).

others.text: Gas, by contrast, rose sharply to reach a peak of 95 TWh in 2010, overtaking coal, before easing slightly to 85 TWh by 2020.

swaps.plainSentence: The bar chart shows the number of people who commuted by car, bus and bicycle in one city between 2005 and 2020.
swaps.formalSentence: The bar chart compares the number of people who commuted by car, bus and bicycle in one city between 2005 and 2020.
swaps.note: Bar charts invite 'compares' – never copy 'shows'.

swaps.plainSentence: The bar chart compares how many people commuted by car, bus and bicycle in one city between 2005 and 2020.
swaps.formalSentence: The bar chart compares the number of people who commuted by car, bus and bicycle in one city between 2005 and 2020.
swaps.note: Turn 'how many' into 'the number of'.

formal: at five-year intervals over the period 2005–2020
swaps.plainSentence: The bar chart compares the number of people who commuted by car, bus and bicycle in one city every five years from 2005 to 2020.
swaps.formalSentence: The bar chart compares the number of people who commuted by car, bus and bicycle in one city at five-year intervals between 2005 and 2020.

in every five years from 2005 to 2020

swaps.plainSentence: The bar chart compares the popularity of three ways of travelling among commuters in one city over the period 2005–2020.
swaps.formalSentence: The bar chart compares the popularity of three modes of transport among commuters in one city over the period 2005–2020.
swaps.note: Paraphrase the topic nouns: ways of travelling → modes of transport.

swaps.plainSentence: Overall, the main thing is that car use declined steadily, while cycling grew in popularity.
swaps.formalSentence: Overall, the most noticeable trend is that car use declined steadily, while cycling grew in popularity.

traps.why: an adverb cannot describe a noun

swaps.note: Overview opener: name the big trend, no figures.

formal: was by far the most popular mode
swaps.plainSentence: The car had the most commuters in the first three years shown, although its lead shrank steadily.
swaps.formalSentence: The car was by far the most popular mode in the first three years shown, although its lead shrank steadily.

traps.text: was far the most popular mode

swaps.note: 'By far' makes a superlative stronger.

swaps.plainSentence: By contrast, more and more people cycled throughout the period.
swaps.formalSentence: By contrast, cycling became increasingly popular throughout the period.
swaps.note: A rise across categories = became increasingly popular.

swaps.plain: stayed more or less the same
swaps.plainSentence: Bus use stayed more or less the same until 2015 but fell in the final year.
swaps.formalSentence: Bus use remained relatively stable until 2015 but fell in the final year.
swaps.note: Little change = remained relatively stable.

formal: By the end of the period
swaps.plainSentence: At the end, the bus had become the least common way to travel to work.
swaps.formalSentence: By the end of the period, the bus had become the least common way to travel to work.

traps.text: In the end of the period

swaps.note: Pair 'by' with the past perfect: by 2020, it had become.

formal: emerged as the most popular option
swaps.plainSentence: Meanwhile, cycling became the number one choice, overtaking the car.
swaps.formalSentence: Meanwhile, cycling emerged as the most popular option, overtaking the car.

traps.text: emerged as the most popular optional
rose as the most popular option

swaps.note: Closing overview line: the change at the top.

formal: the highest by a wide margin
swaps.plainSentence: In 2005, the number of car commuters was the most, at 120,000.
swaps.formalSentence: In 2005, the number of car commuters was by far the highest, at 120,000.
swaps.note: 'The number' is high or low, not 'the most'.

swaps.plainSentence: This was two times the figure for bus users (60,000).
swaps.formalSentence: This was twice the figure for bus users (60,000).
swaps.note: Use 'twice / double', not 'two times'.

swaps.plainSentence: Only 20,000 people cycled to work in 2005.
swaps.formalSentence: A mere 20,000 people cycled to work in 2005.
swaps.note: 'A mere' stresses how small a figure is.

swaps.plainSentence: Over the next fifteen years, the number of car commuters kept going down, reaching 70,000 in 2020.
swaps.formalSentence: Over the next fifteen years, the number of car commuters fell steadily, reaching 70,000 in 2020.
swaps.note: A fall in every category = fell steadily.

swaps.plainSentence: This represented a big fall of more than 40%.
swaps.formalSentence: This represented a considerable decline of more than 40%.
swaps.note: Size adjectives: slight < moderate < considerable < dramatic.

swaps.plainSentence: Car use fell by 50,000 over the period, while the number of cyclists rose by 65,000.
swaps.formalSentence: Car use fell by 50,000 over the period, whereas the number of cyclists rose by 65,000.

traps.why: needs a new sentence or semicolon

swaps.note: 'Whereas' joins two contrasting clauses.

swaps.plain: went up more than four times
swaps.plainSentence: The number of cyclists, on the other hand, went up more than four times, from 20,000 to 85,000.
swaps.formalSentence: The number of cyclists, on the other hand, more than quadrupled, from 20,000 to 85,000.

traps.why: needs a verb: 'rose more than fourfold'

swaps.note: x2 doubled, x3 tripled, x4 quadrupled.

swaps.plainSentence: By 2020, cyclists had gone past car users, at 85,000 compared with 70,000.
swaps.formalSentence: By 2020, cyclists had overtaken car users, at 85,000 compared with 70,000.
swaps.note: By + year → had + past participle.

formal: As far as bus travel is concerned,
swaps.plainSentence: When we look at buses, the figure hovered around 60,000 between 2005 and 2015.
swaps.formalSentence: As far as bus travel is concerned, the figure hovered around 60,000 between 2005 and 2015.

traps.text: As far as bus travel concerned,
As long as bus travel is concerned,

swaps.note: Body 2 opener: switch to the next category.

swaps.plainSentence: In 2015, the number of cyclists was about the same as the number of bus users, at around 60,000.
swaps.formalSentence: In 2015, the number of cyclists was on a par with the number of bus users, at around 60,000.
swaps.note: Two bars almost level = on a par with.

swaps.plain: was used by the fewest people
swaps.plainSentence: By 2020, the bus was used by the fewest people, with only 45,000 commuters.
swaps.formalSentence: By 2020, the bus was the least popular mode, with only 45,000 commuters.
swaps.note: Opposite of 'the most popular' = the least popular.

swaps.plainSentence: Less people drove to work in 2020 than in any earlier year.
swaps.formalSentence: Fewer people drove to work in 2020 than in any earlier year.
swaps.note: Countable nouns take 'fewer', not 'less'.

swaps.plainSentence: In 2020, the car was in second place, with 70,000 commuters.
swaps.formalSentence: In 2020, the car ranked second, with 70,000 commuters.
swaps.note: Ranking categories: ranked first / second / last.

swaps.plainSentence: Cyclists numbered 85,000 in 2020, compared to 70,000 for car users.
swaps.formalSentence: Cyclists numbered 85,000 in 2020, in comparison with 70,000 for car users.
swaps.note: Put two figures side by side in one sentence.

swaps.plainSentence: In 2020, bicycle commuters were more than bus commuters by almost two to one.
swaps.formalSentence: In 2020, bicycle commuters outnumbered bus commuters by almost two to one.
swaps.note: For people or things you can count: outnumbered.

swaps.plainSentence: Meanwhile, the gap between car and bus users got smaller from 60,000 to 25,000.
swaps.formalSentence: Meanwhile, the gap between car and bus users narrowed from 60,000 to 25,000.
swaps.note: A gap narrows or widens.

swaps.plainSentence: Cycling attracted a lot more commuters than the bus in 2020.
swaps.formalSentence: Cycling attracted considerably more commuters than the bus in 2020.
swaps.note: Grade comparatives: slightly / considerably / far more.
